Mechanical blob and digest validation is the independent Codex lane and is neither duplicated nor disputed here. findings.defect: The engineering-register result recorded for the machine-readable artifacts does not bind the artifacts under review, and is not reproducible. canary-verification.json register_json_prose records input_hashes d9acb1f86b61a7bcbc5ead2e310d16e9805d83b9babe06b704d7f807b2a9aa05, ee3aadaa2bc8a750983c763628c26696e52340cada3b4c4535d3119310086837, 23ee536e0bbb7da2204196ce52d1fc956d23e3c9f6373b031d87404e759b1379 and 181c0de86ec172d0f727964b9134d04d2898eed806520249e60edebe84985929 for the canary proposal, the scope record, the vendor source register and the diagnostic characterization. The same receipt's staged_and_scanned_mirror_files records 1a10c0cf..., e7d80942..., 340cd7ff... and e96e0d41... for those same four paths, and the bundle carries the staged digests. The receipt explains only one divergence - 'The verification receipt input is its pre-regeneration version, explicitly hashed here' - and states nothing about the other four. The recorded exit_code 0, the '1 file(s) checked, 0 violation(s)' result and the extracted_prose_sha256 therefore describe superseded content for four of the five declared inputs, while the receipt's own scope line claims coverage of 'All staged canary planning files except this regenerated verification receipt'. Two further gaps compound it. The extractor that produced extracted_prose_sha256 is recorded as script_name SOLVERS-2121-register-json.py with a digest, but it is private SOLVERS coordination evidence rather than a repository artifact, so no reviewer can re-run the recorded extraction_rule against the staged blobs and reproduce the digest. And the checks[] entry for the HTML register run records a command, an exit code and a stdout digest but no input digest, so the plan's own register PASS is likewise unattached to any specific version of the HTML. Checkpoint N6 asked for the extraction rule, input hashes, byte count and script digest, and all four fields are now present; the defect is that the values recorded do not resolve to the tree presented for approval, which is the property the fields exist to establish.
findings.correction: Regenerate the register extraction against the exact staged blobs so that every entry in register_json_prose.input_hashes equals the corresponding entry in staged_and_scanned_mirror_files, and re-record extracted_bytes and extracted_prose_sha256 from that run. Record the HTML input digest alongside the existing stdout digest in the checks[] entry for check-engineering-register.py. Commit the extractor under a repository path, or replace it with a committed equivalent, so the recorded extraction_rule is executable by a reviewer. If one input must legitimately lag its own regeneration, state that exemption per path with its reason, as is already done for the receipt itself, rather than leaving four silent mismatches.

findings.defect: The stored-precision evidence requirement asserts a command adjacency that the pinned source register does not establish, and it is mandatory on every attempt. The HTML states 'Native /CONFIG,STAT output immediately before and after SOLVE will show zero; missing/conflicting status or later override will refuse evidence', the proposal's recovery.stored_precision states 'issue /CONFIG,RESUPREC,0 and retain /CONFIG,STAT immediately before SOLVE and after SOLVE. Both observed states must show RESUPREC0', and execution_evidence lists 'pre/post RESUPREC0 status retained' among the conditions checked at every attempt. The CONFIG-v242 register entry records the RESUPREC value semantics, the config.ans override behaviour and 'STAT reports current settings', but records no fact about the processor level at which /CONFIG may be issued. That omission matters here and nowhere else in the deck: /CONFIG is a Begin-level configuration command, while the two positions named are inside the solution processor (immediately before SOLVE) and inside the solution processor or POST1 (after SOLVE). Obtaining the two captures therefore requires FINISH and re-entry around each STAT, a sequence the proposal does not describe, and which the phrase 'immediately before SOLVE' reads against. Every other command whose placement the plan fixes - SFELIST, FLIST and DLIST before SOLVE in /SOLU, ERESX and OUTRES before solution, PRESOL, PRNSOL and PRRSOL in POST1, *GET, *VWRITE and *CFOPEN anywhere - sits in a processor where it is available. Because the zero control runs first and execution-evidence failures stop immediately at every mesh, an unavailable /CONFIG,STAT at either named point refuses evidence on attempt 1, consumes that attempt and ends the lane before any numerical observation is obtained, with the no-relaxation rule leaving amendment and re-approval as the only route.
findings.correction: Add the processor-availability fact for /CONFIG to the CONFIG-v242 register entry on the same footing as the RESUPREC values, and write the exact command sequence into the proposal - for example FINISH, /CONFIG,STAT, /SOLU, SOLVE, FINISH, /CONFIG,STAT - stating that solution settings persist across the re-entry so NSUBST, AUTOTS, ERESX and OUTRES are unaffected. If a status retrieval is available without leaving the solution processor, name it instead. Add a B1 deck test asserting that both STAT captures are present in the generated deck's expected output positions and that both report RESUPREC 0, and a RED fixture refusing a deck that reports only one.

findings.defect: The byte-empty process-stream gate is frozen at B1 approval while the evidence that would establish whether it is satisfiable is already retained, pinned by digest and readable offline. The proposal's warning_policy.process_streams requires process stderr to be byte-empty and process stdout outside the attributed native output file to be byte-empty, makes any nonempty stream INCOMPLETE even at exit zero, and states that 'an incompatible launcher profile will require a reviewed amendment, never an after-run waiver'. The HTML repeats it and execution_evidence makes 'dedicated process streams empty' mandatory at every attempt. No artifact records any observation of what the launcher this plan intends to reuse actually writes to those streams. Two prior native runs are pinned in canary-scope.json diagnostic_corpus - ansys-2094-canary-20260912T205311Z and ansys-2094-pressure-prep-20260913T021014Z - and the new diagnostic characterization demonstrates those directories are readable offline at byte level, since it records exact byte offsets, body digests and a Python version for four files inside them. Neither the scope record nor the characterization says whether those runs captured process stdout and stderr at all, nor what those captures contained. The plan simultaneously commits to reusing src/digitalmodel/ansys/runner.py 'for the existing batch interface' without characterising that module's stream handling. This is the same defect class that checkpoint N2 closed for diagnostic headings: a strict gate adopted at the approval that freezes it, with the deciding evidence retained and cheap to read. The consequence is not a legitimate INCOMPLETE from the physics; it is an INCOMPLETE on attempt 1 caused by a launcher property knowable before any solver is invoked.
findings.correction: Before B1 approval, record in canary-scope.json or a hashed sidecar whether each pinned prior native run captured process stdout and stderr, and for each capture that exists its byte length and digest, using the same offline reading path the diagnostic characterization already demonstrates. If the retained captures show the launcher emits banner or license text at exit zero, either restrict the gate to byte-empty stderr plus stdout content not matching a frozen launcher-banner grammar hashed at B1, or state the exact launcher invocation and redirection that produces empty streams and test that specification offline against the retained captures. If no prior run captured streams, state that explicitly in the scope record so the gate is adopted as an acknowledged unverified assumption rather than an implied verified one, and keep the existing B1 RED test for a zero-exit nonempty stream.

findings.defect: The two most-read status fields name the wrong correction round, contradicting the plan's own body and the scope record. The HTML header paragraph reads 'B1 approval blocked; R3 inline corrections awaiting exact-current independent review' and the proposal's status field reads 'blocked for B1 approval; R3 inline corrections awaiting exact-current independent review'. The same HTML carries a separate section titled 'Checkpoint corrections for independent review' describing the N1 to N7 work, canary-scope.json review_status reads 'Current checkpoint corrections await exact-current independent review', historical_rounds records 'user-authorized checkpoint R1' at tree e03359e1 as a round after canary R3 at tree 53518eef with status 'current corrections await next exact review', canary-verification.json current_review_coverage names checkpoint R1, and README.md records 'checkpoint corrections under review'. The vendor register handles the same distinction correctly, marking PRESOL, CFOPEN, MSG and NERR as 'R3 inline correction' and CONFIG, SFELIST, FLIST and DLIST as 'current checkpoint correction'. As written, the approval record a reader reaches first describes the reviewed content as one round older than it is, which is a traceability defect in the artifact the user is asked to approve.
findings.correction: Change the HTML header line and the proposal's status field to name the checkpoint corrections under review at this tree, matching canary-scope.json review_status and the README row. Retain the phrase 'R3 inline corrections' only where R3-era provenance is meant, as the vendor register already does.

findings.defect: A hash reference in the diagnostic characterization resolves to nothing at this tree and carries no stated basis. 2026-09-14-issue-2121-diagnostic-characterization.json records scope_sha256 e5c6e25dbf4812392a296c6b39e0e0b62e5944c662432a76ae86a462920c9276, while the staged canary-scope.json is e7d80942fb3d3d847e95f90f0b428dc684a5505690b5451aa5a37efbf25566e9. The two files reference each other - canary-scope.json ends with diagnostic_characterization naming the characterization file - so neither can carry the other's final digest at the same tree. The plan already has a correct convention for exactly this circularity: canary-verification.json states receipt_exclusion, 'This receipt is excluded from its own digest set. A subsequent staged-file scan will include it; no self-hash claim', and canary_R3 F7 in the scope record reasons it out explicitly. No equivalent statement accompanies scope_sha256, so a reader cannot distinguish a deliberate pre-reference pin from a stale or wrong value, and the field is the characterization's only claimed binding to the scope record whose corpus digests it reproduces.
findings.correction: Label scope_sha256 with the version it pins and why it differs from the staged blob, mirroring the receipt_exclusion wording - for example that it pins the scope record as read before the diagnostic_characterization reference was added, with the binding at this tree carried by canary-verification.json. Alternatively drop the field and let the verification receipt's staged_and_scanned_mirror_files carry the binding for both files.

findings.defect: The applied-load audit does not define the expected surface-load database state for the zero control, which is the first attempt executed. The proposal's recovery.load_audit requires SFELIST,ALL,ALL with full ESEL immediately before SOLVE and states the acceptance rule as 'require only intended inner-face pressure with correct sign/magnitude, no outer/top/bottom surface load and no applied nodal force', with B1 RED fixtures that 'will refuse reversed sign, wrong magnitude, wrong face and unsupported/missing load records'. The HTML repeats the same rule without qualification. Case ocv-zero-t60-n16 carries pressure_mpa '0' and runs first under the flow 'N16 zero control first; stop any control or execution/evidence failure'. Its intended inner-face pressure is zero, and no artifact states whether the generated control deck carries an SFE record with value zero on the inner faces or carries no surface-load record at all. Both readings are refusable under the rule as written: a deck with no surface load can be read as a missing load record, and a deck with SFE zero can be read as a surface load that is not the intended inner pressure. Because execution-evidence failures stop immediately and an attempt is consumed at invocation, an ambiguity resolved the wrong way at implementation time ends the canary on attempt 1. This is the one remaining unspecified branch in an audit that is otherwise pinned to named commands and keyed fields.
findings.correction: State the control's expected surface-load database state explicitly in the proposal's load_audit and in the HTML - either that SFELIST reports no surface loads for ocv-zero-t60-n16 and that absence is the required state, or that the control carries SFE pressure zero on the same inner faces as the pressure cases. Add a B1 fixture for that exact case alongside the existing wrong-face, reversed-sign, wrong-magnitude and missing-record fixtures, so the control's audit outcome is established offline rather than at first invocation.
